feedback: Reject. (1) Predicate inconsistencies: (u0, key_lost) -> u0 conflicts with the else self-loop and overlaps (u0, blocker_moved & key_lost) -> u0, i.e. moving the blocker and losing the key simultaneously would claim a -0.1 reward but the reward function lists only (u0, key_lost, u0) -> -0.1 and (u0, blocker_moved, u1) -> 0.1, so the (u0, blocker_moved & key_lost) transition has no matching reward (rewards must be total over all non-self-loop transitions). Similarly (u2, blocker_moved & door_open & has_door_key) and (u2, door_open & has_door_key) are redundant with (u2, door_open) -> u3 and have no listed reward entries. (u0, blocker_moved & !key_lost & key_lost) is unsatisfiable (contradictory guard) and should be removed. (2) Unreachable state: u4 is never entered from any transition, so it and its rows are dead code; if it encodes an alternative path (e.g. key picked up before the ball), there is no transition from u0/u1 into it, meaning the key-first route (149/300 episodes) collapses onto the same path — acceptable semantically only if intended, but currently u4 serves no purpose and should be deleted or connected. (3) Dense-progress concern: the task says 'try not to drop the key while the door is still closed'; the -0.1 penalty on key_lost is present in u0, u1, u2, which covers the door-closed phase correctly, and no penalty after door_open — good. However, the ordered-transition coverage is incomplete: dropping the ball back in front of the door makes blocker_moved false; from u1 there is no (u1, !blocker_moved) -> u0 regression, so the RM latches blocker progress permanently even though blocker_moved is explicitly a non-latching condition and the environment permits re-blocking. Add an explicit regression (u1, key_lost & !blocker_moved) exists, but plain ball re-drop without key loss is unhandled — the agent could regress blocker_moved and stay in u1, then reach u2 via has_door_key without the ball moved; from u2, door_open can then fire, violating the constraint that door_open cannot become true before blocker_moved. This is a semantic fidelity violation of the environment constraint. (4) Reward bookkeeping: (u1, key_lost & blocker_moved, u1) -> -0.1 exists, but the corresponding transition with no reward for (u1, key_lost & !blocker_moved) -> u0 (the penalty transition back to u0) is missing a reward entry — every transition in the transition function needs a reward entry (0 is fine, but it must be listed). (5) Minor: FINAL_STATES is present and u5 declared/accepting — that header requirement is met; overall format is otherwise close to the paper format. Fix the satisfiability/redundancy issues, make rewards total, handle the blocker_moved regression from u1, and remove or wire up u4.

feedback:
Several issues.

1. Ordering/progression fault (critical): from u2 the only forward transition is door_open & !key_lost. That is fine, but the else self-loop allows door_open to become true while key_lost is true? Actually key_lost & door_open is impossible (constrained), so no problem there. However, in u2 a key_lost with blocker_moved keeps the agent in u2 even though the key is gone and the door still closed — the agent can no longer ever reach u3 without picking the key back up (has_door_key is only checked in u1). Once in u2, picking the key back up is invisible to the RM, so opening the door after re-acquiring the key still transitions correctly via door_open & !key_lost (key_lost is one-step only), so this is acceptable. But in u1/u2 the regression on key_lost & blocker_moved keeps too much credit — see next point.

2. Ordered transition coverage for key_lost regressions: key_lost & blocker_moved in u1/u2 self-loops with small penalties is reasonable, but from u2 the key_lost & !blocker_moved -> u0 reset erases door_open progress... actually door_open cannot be true with key_lost, so a drop while closed after the ball moved is genuinely a partial regression; resetting to u0 forces redoing has_door_key but not blocker_moved? u0 requires blocker_moved to advance, which the agent may not need to redo (the ball stays moved). Wait — blocker_moved may have turned false (ball dropped back in front of the door), in which case u0 is correct; but if the ball was dropped elsewhere, blocker_moved stays true and u0 forces a redundant blocker_moved event that will never occur (u0's only progress edge requires blocker_moved & !key_lost; blocker_moved is not an event, so if it is already true and stays true, no transition labels with blocker_moved can fire because label deltas trigger on truth changes... actually ARM-FM labels fire on current-step proposition valuations, so a persistent blocker_moved=true can satisfy u0's edge immediately, sending the agent to u1 — that works). Still, from u0, if blocker_moved is persistently true but the agent regains the key, u0 -> u1 fires correctly. Reachability is OK.

3. Missing constraint coverage: the RM never enforces 'door_open before target_picked_up' — fine, structure does (u3 requires door_open). But nothing forces has_door_key before door_open in the structure beyond u2 gating; acceptable.

4. Reward safety/compactness: rewards are bounded and dense via progress edges; the u1 key_lost & blocker_moved -0.1 and u2 -0.1 penalties are unbounded in count but the event can fire repeatedly (drop/pickup cycles), allowing reward farming of -0.1? Negative, so no farming; safe.

5. Final states header: FINAL_STATES: u4 is present and u4 is accepting (else self-loop, no exit) — OK.

6. Format: transitions use else self-loops; else self-loops have no reward entries — the spec requires a reward for every transition, including else self-loops. Missing reward entries for (u0, else, u0), (u1, else, u1), (u2, else, u2), (u3, else, u3), (u4, else, u4). Also (u0, key_lost & !blocker_moved, u0) has reward -0.1 but this self-loop transition is not listed in TRANSITION_FUNCTION (it is: '(u0, key_lost & !blocker_moved) -> u0' — present, OK).

7. Main blocking flaw: in u2, the agent may legitimately drop the key while the ball has been dropped elsewhere (key_lost & blocker_moved) and must re-pick it; the RM stays in u2, then door_open & !key_lost advances — fine. But if the agent drops the key while the ball was dropped back in front of the door (key_lost & !blocker_moved), it resets to u0 where progression requires blocker_moved as a currently-true proposition; since blocker_moved is a condition that may still be true, the edge fires immediately — acceptable. The genuinely problematic case: u2 -> u0 reset loses the u2 reward potential after merely dropping the key, over-penalizing (regression is explicit but the task only says 'try not to', severity mismatch is minor).

The decisive rejection reason: incomplete REWARD_FUNCTION (missing entries for all else self-loop transitions), which makes the reward function partial and violates the required one-to-one transition/reward pairing.

feedback: The candidate RM accepts, but it is semantically unsound and over-rewards. Problems: (1) In u0, only `blocker_moved` is recognized, but the environment explicitly allows the agent to pick up the key first (`has_door_key` fires while `blocker_moved` is still false, since the key is reachable without moving the ball). A trace showing the key-acquired-first path would get stuck in u0 with the transition (u0, has_door_key) undefined and fall to the else self-loop, never reaching u2, so door_open (which requires has_door_key) would never be detected as progress. The RM must model has_door_key happening before blocker_moved. (2) Similarly, in u0 there is no handling for `key_lost` (e.g., if the agent picks up the key then drops it while the ball is still in place, key_lost fires but u0's else self-loop just stays in u0 with reward 0, which is fine, but it also means the agent has to re-do has_door_key, which is still not modeled in u0). (3) In u1, the transition (u1, key_lost) -> u1 is wrong: key_lost means the agent LOST the key it had while the door is closed, so it should move back to u0 (or a state without the key), not stay in u1. Also there is no transition (u1, !blocker_moved) -> u0 even though blocker_moved is a condition that can become false again when the ball is dropped back in front of the door. (4) In u2, key_lost should not be possible since door_open is required to enter u2, and key_lost requires door_open to be false; the (u2, key_lost) transition is dead/incorrect per the proposition constraints. (5) In u2, `!blocker_moved` -> u0 is a regression that over-penalizes: `blocker_moved` is just a condition about the cell in front of the door, and its becoming false after the door is already open does not invalidate progress (the agent could have dropped the ball back there, or the ball was never dropped at all after the door opened). This state should not regress to u0. (6) Reward density is broken: the else self-loops in u1 and u2 give reward 0, so there are long stretches with no dense progress signal. Rewards should be given for progress towards the subgoal within each state (e.g., a small positive reward for `has_door_key` in u1, `door_open` in u2) rather than only at the exact state-transitioning event. (7) The ordered-transition coverage is incomplete: there is no way to represent the valid sequence key-first-then-ball (u0 --has_door_key--> u1 --blocker_moved--> u2 --door_open--> u3), which is required by the environment mechanics. (8) FINAL_STATES header is present and u3 is declared and accepting, which is good, but the semantic gaps above prevent acceptance.

feedback: The candidate is close but fails ordered transition coverage at u3. The task requires: blocker moved, key acquired, then door open, then target picked up. u3 is entered after both blocker_moved and has_door_key hold (in either order), which is correct given constraints, but u3's transitions only check target_picked_up and regressions (!door_open, key_lost); they never check door_open. Since u3 is reachable from u0 via has_door_key when the ball is still in place, and from u2 via has_door_key, the agent in u3 must still open the door — the machine must gate target_picked_up on door_open having occurred, e.g. a state u4 (door_open reached with blocker moved and key history) leading to a final state. (u1, has_door_key, u2) -> 0.2
(u1, !blocker_moved, u0) -> -0.1
(u1, key_lost, u1) -> -0.1
(u2, door_open & !key_lost, u4) -> 0.4
(u2, key_lost, u2) -> -0.1
(u3, blocker_moved, u2) -> 0.2
(u3, !blocker_moved, u1) -> -0.1
(u3, key_lost, u3) -> -0.1
(u4, target_picked_up, u5) -> 1.0
(u4, !door_open, u2) -> -0.2
(u4, key_lost, u4) -> -0.1
feedback: The RM correctly encodes the three subgoals (move blocker, get key, open door, pick up box) with order variants (u0->u1/u2->u2->u4->u5), key_lost penalty self-loops, and regressions when the ball is dropped back (!blocker_moved) or the door re-closed (!door_open), so the structure is largely sound. However, the transition and reward functions are inconsistent and incomplete. (1) Several transitions exist in the transition function but have no reward entry: (u2, door_open & !key_lost, u4) has reward but (u2, key_lost, u2), (u3, key_lost, u3), (u4, key_lost, u4) have rewards yet (u2, door_open) is listed once, and (u1, key_lost, u1) is penalized while the transition (u1, !blocker_moved) to u0 with reward -0.1 is fine — but the transition (u3, has_door_key) case is missing entirely: u3 is reached via has_door_key from u0, yet u3 has no self-loop for carrying the key; if the agent in u3 picks up the ball, (u3, blocker_moved) fires (true) and goes to u2, which is correct, but while in u3 nothing stops an issue. (2) More critically, (u1, key_lost) -> u1 cannot occur in u1 before the key is ever picked up (key_lost requires has_door_key previously), and the reward entry (u1, key_lost, u1) -> -0.1 likewise applies only in u1/u3 pre-door paths where the key was picked up then dropped — those are fine — but the RM has no transition for has_door_key turning true while already in u2 (agent moves blocker first, then picks up key: (u2, has_door_key) needs a self-loop reward; currently the else self-loop covers it, which is acceptable but means no penalty for holding the key in u2 — acceptable). (3) Semantic issue: the (u0, key_lost) -> u0 transition and reward (u0,...) missing — key_lost cannot fire in u0 since has_door_key was false; harmless dead entry but the reward entry (u0, key_lost) is absent while (u1,u3) have it: inconsistent but not incorrect. (4) Final issue: the reward entry (u0, blocker_moved & has_door_key, u2) -> 0.2 equals the sum of individual rewards 0.1+0.1, which is consistent; (u1, !blocker_moved, u0) -> -0.1 correctly penalizes regression. The main defect is that the reward function omits entries for transitions that give 0 reward implicitly — if implicit 0 is allowed this is fine, but the (u2, door_open & !key_lost, u4) reward of 0.4 with final reward 1.0 gives a sensible dense-ish schedule. Rejected because the FINAL_STATES check passes but the (u4, !door_open) regression to u2 loses all progress and the agent could cycle door_open without penalty for re-toggling the door shut (doors cannot be relocked, per constraints, so !door_open in u4 is unreachable — dead transition/reward that contradicts the stated constraint 'Cannot: relock a door'; this dead entry is minor). Given the mostly sound design but the dead (u4, !door_open) entry conflicting with the environment's no-relock constraint and inconsistent reward coverage, reject pending cleanup.
